newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura sees 10.5 pct profit rise at Japan firms.
newsitem.headline: Nomura sees 10.5 pct profit rise at Japan firms.

text.p: Nomura Research Institute Ltd said on Monday it expects parent current profits at Japanese firms to rise by an average of 10.5 percent in the year to March 31 compared with last business year.
It said it would be the second year in a row of double-digit growth.
Nomura Research, a research unit of Nomura Securities Co Ltd, expected the companies' current profit to show a year-on-year rise of 8.3 percent in 1997/1998, it said in its report.
It sees the companies' parent current profit rising 8.9 percent year-on-year in 1998/99.
The report covered major Japanese companies from all industry sectors, except the financial sector, Nomura Research said.
Nomura Research said the expected profit rise in 1996/97 was due to the weak yen and Japan's economic recovery.
But it said that its latest forecast of a 10.5 percent rise was slightly lower than the previous forecast of 10.7 percent announced late last year.
Nomura Research raised the firms' parent current profit forecast for 1997/98 from its previous forecast of a 6.0 percent rise, due to the yen's weakness.

Nomura Research said that its previous forecast was based on an assumption that the dollar would average 110 yen in 1996/97 and 113 yen in 1997/98, but its latest forecast was based an assumption that the dollar would be 112 yen in 1996/97 and 120 yen in 1997/98.
Nomura Research changed its forecast for the electronics and precision machinery sectors' current profit for 1997/98 to growth of 9.4 percent from its previous forecast of a 0.8 percent fall.
It raised its outlook for growth in car industry profits in 1997/98 to a rise of 13.0 percent from its previous forecast of a 3.7 percent rise.

Nomura Research said its estimate for 1998/99 was based on an assumption that the dollar would average 118 yen. It added that the yen would start moderately rising after the dollar reaches its peak in the April-June period of this year.
In 1998/99, the electronics and precision machinery sectors' parent current profit should grow year-on-year by 16.6 percent, Nomura Research said.
It sees the steel sector's current profit in 1998/99 growing 24.3 percent year-on-year.
Nomura Research said it expected group current profit of the steel companies to grow 13.4 percent in 1996/97, and another 11.9 percent in 1997/98.
It previously estimated the companies' group current profit rise at 11.7 percent in 1996/97 and 8.9 percent in 1997/98.
